title: The Disabled soldier in the ward
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：disabled　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 disabled 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 the elder wrote of ① a disabled soldier in the ward in the memoir, and everybody in the village said at once that it was ② so disabled that nobody in the village would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the elder, who never explained anything, had done it with great care and gone home; it was the disabled ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the disabled soldier in the ward that anybody there had ever seen, or so the memoir for November 1956 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too disabled to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the youth who had come to help; the disabled ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a disabled lift at the station, and said that no youth in his right mind would call it ⑥ as disabled as the lift at the station they had once had in the old village. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was disabled or not, and he said so.

By 1969 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the memoir. What the line asked for was ⑦ something disabled, and nothing besides. The youth from the next village called the whole plan ⑧ quite disabled; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the memoir kept the names of the disabled ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1972, on the same day, she wrote of another disabled soldier in the ward in the same memoir, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less disabled than anybody had expected. ⑩ The disabled lift at the station that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1974, was the one she could never quite name; the disabled ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 残疾（前置定语 a disabled soldier in the ward：1962 年长者在回忆录里记下的那件残疾的军人）
B. adj. 残疾／残障（两处加强说法：so disabled that … 与 no less disabled than …）
C. adj. 残疾／残障（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 残疾（表语 too disabled to do：母亲觉得它太残疾，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 残障（前置定语 a disabled lift at the station：叔叔把整件事称作一桩残障的升降梯）
F. adj. 残障（同级比较 as disabled as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩车站的升降梯相比）
G. adj. 残障（后置定语 something disabled：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 残障（受程度副词修饰 quite disabled：那位后生的评价）

items.q: a disabled soldier in the ward
the disabled soldier in the ward that
a disabled lift at the station
The disabled lift at the station that

answers.why: disabled 意为“残疾”，1962 年长者在回忆录里记下的是“一件残疾的军人”，此处作前置定语 a disabled soldier in the ward。
disabled 意为“残疾”，此处用 so disabled that 结构，说它残疾到村子里没人敢靠近。
disabled 意为“残疾”，回忆录上 十一月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的残疾病房里的军人，等于最高级的说法。
disabled 意为“残疾”，母亲认为这件东西“太残疾了，谁也用不上”，too disabled to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
disabled 意为“残障”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩残障的升降梯”，此处作前置定语 a disabled lift at the station。
disabled 意为“残障”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩车站的升降梯一样残障”，同级比较用 as disabled as。
disabled 意为“残障”，回忆录上那半行字要的是“残障的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something disabled。
disabled 意为“残障”，邻村子来的那位后生认为这套计划“相当残障”，quite 修饰原级 disabled。
disabled 意为“残障”，no less disabled than 表示“其残障不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之残障不亚于任何人的预料。
disabled 意为“残障”，母亲 1974 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的残障升降梯”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1962 年，长者在回忆录里记下了一件残疾的军人。（a disabled soldier in the ward）
它残疾到村子里没有一个人敢靠近。（so disabled that …）
母亲觉得它太残疾，谁也用不上。（too disabled to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩残障的升降梯。（a disabled lift at the station）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩车站的升降梯一样残障。（as disabled as …）
到了 1969 年，回忆录上只剩半行字：要的是一件残障的东西。（something disabled）
answers: In 1962 the elder wrote of a disabled soldier in the ward in the memoir.
It was so disabled that nobody in the village would go near it.
My mother thought it too disabled to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a disabled lift at the station.
He said nobody would call it as disabled as the lift at the station they had once had.
By 1969 the memoir asked for nothing but something disabled.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 disabled 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1962 the elder wrote of a disabled soldier in the ward in the memoir, and nobody forgot it.
It was the disabled soldier in the ward that anybody there had ever seen, or so the memoir says.
My mother thought it too disabled to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a disabled lift at the station, and nobody argued with him.
The youth from the next village called the plan quite disabled, and everybody laughed.
The disabled ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
